newsitem.title: USA: US House conferees won't drop deminimis rule.
newsitem.headline: US House conferees won't drop deminimis rule.

text.p: U.S. House tax conferees, as expected, told Senate negotiators Friday that they will not drop a proposal to broadly scale back the two-percent de minimis rule, a 25-page House document said Friday.
The statement appeared in a new counteroffer that House conferees sent Senate negotiators as both sides attempt to iron out differences in tax cut bills passed recently by the two chambers.
House tax conferees on Friday also refused to bow to the Senate on other muni-related differences, according to the document.

House panelists, for instance, again rejected the Senate's proposal for full repeal of the $150 million volume cap on 501(c)(3) bonds. The House wants to raise the volume cap only by $50 million over five years, for a total of $200 million.

House conferees also refused to accept a Senate provision to increase from $5 million to $10 million the arbitrage rebate exception for small issuers of public school infrastructure bonds, the document says.
And House panelists refused to adopt the Senate's proposal to hike from $10 million to $20 million the ceiling on capital expenditures by firms issuing small-issue industrial development bonds.
House and Senate conferees also remain at a stalemate on varying plans to assist the financially struggling District of Columbia.
The two houses have compromised on two muni-related issues. The Senate accepted a House proposal to allow refunding of certain tax-exempt Virgin Island bonds.

And both chambers said they would waive mortgage revenue bond purchase price and income limits for people buying homes in presidentially declared disaster areas for up to two years after disasters occur.
